how_it_wins:
You win with one trigger — and, new in v2, you accrue with one ping. Engine one is unchanged: Gishath, Sun's Avatar hits a player, you reveal that many cards from the top of your library, and every Dinosaur among them lands on the battlefield for free. Thirty-four bodies (deck-facts: 34 threat:body roles in 65 nonland spells) keep the reveal dense, and stack 001 prices one clean 7-damage connection at five bodies, three draws, and a discover 6 — one attack that replaces a turn cycle of casting. Engine two is what the seven-card swap block bought, and it is checker-verified on the exact board the block creates: the enrage ping web. With Forerunner of the Empire out, any Dinosaur entering lets you deal 1 damage to each creature, and stack 005 resolves what a single ping is worth — an opponent's 1/1 dead to state-based actions, their 3/3 exiled under Trapjaw Tyrant, a card off Ripjaw Raptor, a tapped Forest off Ranging Raptors, and a Polyraptor copy token whose own entry re-arms the trigger. No combat, no 8 mana, stoppable at every link. The goldfish says the web is now the deck's most reliable engine: enrage pieces are drawn by turn 6 in 72.1% of games, against 62.0% for the Dinosaur payoff engines.

The honest cost of the headline plan is still the number 8. In the goldfish model the commander's mean cast turn is 7.982 (median 8), and only 8.8% of games cast him by turn 6 — but the simulator explicitly models neither the cost reducers nor the swap block's two accelerants, so treat 7.98 as the ceiling of the problem, not your expectation. Real games beat it three ways: ramp (87.1% of games see ramp or fixing by turn 6, mean turn 2.0 — Cultivate, Kodama's Reach, Nature's Lore, Skyshroud Claim, five rocks, the dorks), the cheat/reducer layer (56.5% by turn 6 — Urza's Incubator and Otepec Huntmaster shave the cast; Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual, and Descendants' Path skip it entirely), and the new big mana: Selvala taps for X equal to your greatest power, which any maindeck 5/5 makes 5-plus, and Regal Behemoth doubles every land tap while you hold the crown. How many turns those two actually shave is deliberately unstated — no artifact quantifies it yet. The deck-facts traps stand: Unclaimed Territory's mana casts creature spells only and can never activate Belbe's Portal or Monster Manual; Secluded Courtyard pays creature-source abilities — Zacama yes, the artifacts no.

One honest sentence belongs in every Rule 0 conversation: the bracket report computes floor 4 because the combo database tags Polyraptor + Forerunner of the Empire as a two-card infinite, and stack 003 verified that exact pairing as bounded — a maximum of seven tokens, reached only by declining a trigger, self-terminating when Forerunner dies to its own sweep — so present the 4, show the verified stack, and let the table land on 3.

What the swaps did not change is the wrath math. The Gishath board still arrives as one sweeper-sized package — the trigger is the wave — so the swing rules govern: attack only when Gishath can actually connect (his own vigilance, trample, and haste do most of it; Rogue's Passage and Kessig Wolf Run force the rest — the connection kit is drawn by turn 6 in 50.9% of games) and preferably with protection held (49.3% by turn 6; Flawless Maneuver is free with your commander out, which makes it the swing-turn card). Assume the sweeper. What v2 adds is a better morning after: the ping web restarts at two cards — Forerunner plus any Dinosaur — while the Gishath plan restarts at 8-plus-tax, and Ranging Raptors' lands and Ripjaw's draws stay banked through the wrath. Pantlaza, Sun-Favored plus the draw engines remain the other rebuild. The one soft point to guard: every web line routes through Forerunner of the Empire, a 1/3 Human Soldier that none of the deck's tribal shields cover — only the board-wide protection instants do.

combo_lines.001: This is the deck's core action resolved precisely once, and the lesson is trigger ordering. Gishath connects for 7; the stipulated reveal holds four Dinosaur creature cards (Regisaur Alpha, Ripjaw Raptor, Carnage Tyrant, and Ravenous Sailback — the last since moved to the bench; the ordering lesson is identical with any fourth Dinosaur) and three cards that bottom. All four Dinosaurs enter simultaneously — with Pantlaza, Sun-Favored and Garruk's Uprising on the battlefield, that's nine triggers, and you control the order of every one. The play: put Carnage Tyrant's Pantlaza trigger on top so the once-per-turn discover resolves first at X=6, and put Regisaur Alpha's token trigger on the bottom, so the 3/3 arrives after the discover is spent and re-triggers nothing (it misses Uprising at power 3, and per rule 603.2h Pantlaza's used-up ability doesn't even trigger). Net: five bodies, three draws, a discover 6 — all hasty, all too late for this combat without an extra-combat effect.
combo_lines.002: This scenario exists to stop a mistake, and it is the reason the swap block stopped at seven: Marauding Raptor + Polyraptor is a DRAW-MACHINE, not a win condition. The line was verified when both cards sat on the bench; today Polyraptor is maindeck and Marauding Raptor stays benched BECAUSE of this verdict. Every trigger in the loop is mandatory: Polyraptor resolves, Marauding pings it for 2, the 5/5 shrugs it off and copies itself, the copy enters, the ping is forced again, forever. The deck still has no exit — no sacrifice outlet, no instant-speed way to remove Marauding Raptor — so the loop either gets broken by an opponent, on their terms and at a token count they choose, or CR 732.4 / 104.4b end the game in a draw for the whole table. Never present this pair as a wincon, and never sleeve them together without first adding a loop-breaker you control.
combo_lines.003: The same Polyraptor engine with the safety catch installed — and, as of v2, entirely maindeck. Forerunner of the Empire's trigger is 'you MAY have this creature deal 1 damage to each creature' — optional, once per Dinosaur entry — so unlike stack 002 you hold the off switch at every link. The verified maximum is 7 Polyraptor tokens (8 Polyraptors total), and reaching it takes real piloting: you must DECLINE one intermediate trigger so a second enrage token is on the battlefield before the final sweep — saying yes to everything caps you at 6. The chain self-terminates when Forerunner dies to its own third 1-damage sweep, damage accumulating on its 1/3 body, and it clears opposing small creatures along the way. This is also the pairing the combo database tags infinite — the tag that computes the bracket floor of 4 — and this stack is the substance of the counter-argument: bounded, controllable, and stopped by its own physics at seven.
combo_lines.004: The full package is maindeck as of v2, and it is a one-sided apocalypse. Blasphemous Act deals 13 to each creature; Temple Altisaur prevents all but 1 of that to each of your OTHER Dinosaurs; Wrathful Raptors throws every point your Dinosaurs are dealt at a non-Dinosaur target. The verified accounting has one correction of scale: Temple Altisaur is not 'another Dinosaur' to itself, so it eats the full 13 and dies — but last known information still converts its death into a 13-point redirect. Your other three Dinosaurs take exactly 1 each and throw 1 each. And because state-based actions destroy every lethally damaged creature BEFORE the redirect triggers go on the stack, the opponents' boards are already gone when you choose targets — players are the only legal ones. Total: 16 redirected at one opponent, board swept on your side of a 1-damage haircut. From 26 life that's 10 remaining — devastating, but not lethal by itself.
combo_lines.005: The v2 headline, verified on the exact board the swap block creates. Itzquinth, Firstborn of Gishath enters; Forerunner of the Empire offers its optional ping and you say yes — 1 damage to each creature, all eight of them, Forerunner included. State-based actions kill the opponent's 1/1 token BEFORE any trigger goes on the stack; then exactly four enrage triggers — Trapjaw Tyrant, Ripjaw Raptor, Ranging Raptors, Polyraptor — stack in the order you choose, and Trapjaw's target is picked as its trigger goes on the stack, so the already-dead token can never eat the exile: the 3/3 does. The yield of one ping: a dead 1/1, an exiled 3/3 (held until Trapjaw leaves), a Ripjaw draw, a tapped Forest off Ranging Raptors (a land entering is not a Dinosaur — Forerunner does not re-trigger), and a Polyraptor copy whose own entry re-arms Forerunner with a genuinely new, genuinely optional trigger. The verified close is a decline: the 'you may' is chosen on resolution (rule 603.5), and saying no banks the full yield at a cost of 1 damage marked on each of your creatures — all surviving, all clean again at cleanup.

card_roles.Gishath, Sun's Avatar: The commander and the entire payoff, compressed: combat damage to a player reveals that many cards and free-rolls every Dinosaur among them onto the battlefield. Vigilance, trample, and haste mean the swing happens the turn he lands — stack 001 prices one connection at five bodies, three draws, and a discover 6.
card_roles.Akroma's Will: The swing-turn overload: with your commander out you choose both modes, and flying plus double strike on a Gishath board is usually lethal while indestructible and protection blank the response. One of five board-wide protection pieces (49% held by turn 6).
card_roles.Alpine Meadow: Tapped R/W snow dual. Covers the deck's two thinnest colours at the cost of a turn.
card_roles.Arcane Signet: Any-colour rock for the three-colour pip spread (G 54 / W 23 / R 19 total pips ride heavily on the 13 nonland producers).
card_roles.Austere Command: The flexible sweeper: its modal split (mana value 3 or less vs 4 or greater) is built for this deck — most of your Dinosaurs are 4+, most ramp dorks are not, so choose modes to keep your top end standing.
card_roles.Beast Within: Any-permanent answer at instant speed. The 3/3 Beast the opponent gets is a rounding error against your board.
card_roles.Belbe's Portal: Cheat piece: {3}, {T} puts a Dinosaur from your hand straight onto the battlefield — the tax-proof route past the 8-mana problem. Mind the trap: neither Unclaimed Territory nor Secluded Courtyard can pay its activation.
card_roles.Blasphemous Act: The catch-up sweeper that your own board discounts to {R}, and one third of the verified stack-004 package — now all maindeck: with Temple Altisaur out your Dinosaurs take 1 each while everything else takes 13, and Wrathful Raptors throws the accounting at a player.
card_roles.Bonehoard Dracosaur: Draw engine with a body: two impulse cards every upkeep, plus a 3/1 Dinosaur or a Treasure depending on what it exiles. Part of the cheapest-rebuild package after a wrath.
card_roles.Boros Charm: Modal protection: indestructible for all permanents beats most sweepers, double strike turns a Gishath connection into a 14-card reveal, and 4 to the face closes games.
card_roles.Boros Signet: R/W fixing rock — the deck's two lightest land colours (R 12, W 9 sources against 36/36/36 targets).
card_roles.Bronzebeak Foragers: Multiplayer removal on a Dinosaur body: exiles up to one nonland permanent per opponent until it leaves, and can pay {X}{W} to make an exile permanent while gaining life.
card_roles.Canopy Vista: G/W battle land — untapped once you control two basics, which the basic-heavy ramp suite makes routine.
card_roles.Carnage Tyrant: The uncounterable, hexproof, trampling 7/6 — the free-roll you most want off a Gishath reveal (in stack 001 it carries the discover-6 Pantlaza trigger) and the threat control decks cannot answer cleanly.
card_roles.Cinder Glade: R/G battle land; untapped with two basics.
card_roles.City of Brass: Any-colour fixing at 1 damage per tap — a fair price in a 40-life format for a deck with W/R pips on a green mana base.
card_roles.Clifftop Retreat: R/W check land; untapped with a Mountain or Plains.
card_roles.Command Tower: The best land in the deck: any commander colour, always untapped.
card_roles.Congregation at Dawn: Top-stack rigging: three creature cards on top in any order — cast it before a Gishath connection and the free-roll stops being random. Setup, not a combo; the full line still needs a stack scenario.
card_roles.Cultivate: Core ramp (87% of games see ramp/fixing by turn 6, mean turn 2.0): a basic to the battlefield and one to hand.
card_roles.Curious Altisaur: Typal draw engine: every Dinosaur that connects draws a card, which turns the free-rolled army's next swing into a fistful of cards.
card_roles.Descendants' Path: The repeatable cheat: every upkeep, a revealed Dinosaur creature card gets cast free. With 34 Dinosaur bodies in 99, the hit rate is real, and casting (not just putting) matters for cast triggers.
card_roles.Eerie Interlude: Mass-blink protection with upside: dodges a sweeper at instant speed, then returns the board at end step — and re-entering Dinosaurs mean fresh ETB triggers. Whether Pantlaza's once-per-turn discover can fire off the return needs a stack scenario before you count on it.
card_roles.Enlightened Tutor: One white mana finds Urza's Incubator, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual, Descendants' Path, Garruk's Uprising, or Mirari's Wake — it tutors the cheat/reducer layer, the deck's real accelerant.
card_roles.Etali, Primal Storm: Attack-trigger card advantage off everyone's library — four free spells per swing at a four-player table, and a prime Gishath free-roll since he arrives hasty under Regisaur Alpha or the commander's own timing.
card_roles.Exotic Orchard: Any colour an opponent's land could produce — near-perfect fixing at a Commander table.
card_roles.Flawless Maneuver: The swing-turn card: free with your commander out, indestructible for the team. Hold it through your own attack and through the wrath you should be assuming.
card_roles.Forbidden Orchard: Any-colour fixing that gifts an opponent a 1/1 Spirit per tap — trivial against this deck's board sizes.
card_roles.Forerunner of the Empire: New in v2 and the hub of the ping web: its ETB tutors any Dinosaur to the top of your library — rigging the next Gishath reveal or Descendants' Path upkeep — and every Dinosaur ETB after that offers an OPTIONAL 1 damage to each creature, the trigger that drives stacks 003 and 005. It is a 1/3 Human Soldier, and that is the web's soft point: it stands outside every tribal shield in the deck — Temple Altisaur prevents damage only to other Dinosaurs, the typal lands' mana names Dinosaurs, Gishath's reveal free-rolls only Dinosaurs — its own sweep hits it (1 of 3 in stack 005; dead to its own third sweep in stack 003), and only the board-wide protection instants cover it. Opponents who read the board kill the 1/3 first.
card_roles.Forest: Eight copies: the deck's heaviest basic, matching the green pip weight and the Forest-typed ramp (Nature's Lore, Skyshroud Claim).
card_roles.Garruk's Uprising: Draw engine plus the trample anthem: nearly every body in the deck has power 4 or greater, so it draws on entry and on every threat after — in stack 001 it drew 3 off one connection.
card_roles.Ghalta and Mavren: Attack-trigger token engine: an X/X trampling Dinosaur matching your biggest other attacker, or a squad of lifelinkers, every combat.
card_roles.Ghalta, Primal Hunger: The 12/12 that costs {G}{G} on a developed board — its cost reduction reads the same board Gishath builds, so it often lands the turn after the trigger for nearly free.
card_roles.Heroic Intervention: Two-mana hexproof plus indestructible for everything — the cheapest full answer to both sweepers and targeted removal. Part of the 49%-by-turn-6 protection suite.
card_roles.Huatli, Poet of Unity // Roar of the Fif: Early ramp body that fetches a basic on entry, then transforms into a Saga whose first chapter creates two 3/3 Dinosaurs — a mid-game engine hiding in a three-drop. Face-up she contributes only green to the board (deck-facts: front_face G) even though the card is Naya.
card_roles.Hulking Raptor: A ward-2 ritual on legs: {G}{G} every first main phase is two free mana toward the 8-drop, on a 5/5 body that also blocks.
card_roles.Hunter's Insight: Aim it at an unblocked Gishath and a 7-damage connection also draws 7 cards on top of the reveal. Instant speed means you commit after blocks.
card_roles.Intrepid Paleontologist: Any-colour dork with a graveyard-hate rider that doubles as recursion: it can exile your own dead Dinosaurs and let you cast them later (with a finality counter).
card_roles.Itzquinth, Firstborn of Gishath: A hasty two-drop that brings its own enrage-shaped removal: pay {2} on entry and one of your Dinosaurs fights downward. The deck's cheapest way to bring its own damage — and in stack 005 it is the entering Dinosaur that arms the whole ping web.
card_roles.Jetmir's Garden: The Naya triome: enters tapped but fixes all three colours, and cycles for {3} when you're flooded.
card_roles.Kessig Wolf Run: Land-slot reach: {X}{R}{G} pumps and grants trample — mana into damage in the late game, and a way to force the last points through chump blocks.
card_roles.Kodama's Reach: Core ramp, functionally Cultivate copies five and six through Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim: land on battlefield, land in hand.
card_roles.Krosan Verge: A land that ramps: sacrifice for a Forest and a Plains — and it fetches nonbasic Forests/Plains like the battle lands, not just basics.
card_roles.Mirari's Wake: The double-duty enchantment: +1/+1 for the team and every land taps for double — the single biggest jump toward casting Gishath a full two turns early.
card_roles.Monster Manual // Zoological Study: Repeatable cheat: {1}{G}, {T} puts any creature from hand onto the battlefield, and the Zoological Study adventure digs one back out of your library first. Like Belbe's Portal, its activation cannot be paid by either typal land.
card_roles.Mountain: Five copies, feeding R 12 land sources — the thinnest colour still needs its basics for the check and battle lands.
card_roles.Myriad Landscape: Slow land-slot ramp: sacrifices for two basics that share a type. A fine turn-two play in a deck this hungry for mana.
card_roles.Nature's Lore: Two-mana Forest ramp, untapped — and it can fetch Canopy Vista or Cinder Glade for fixing, not just a basic.
card_roles.Otepec Huntmaster: Cost reducer and haste enabler in one drop: Dinosaur spells cost {1} less and its tap grants haste — both halves of the plan on one fragile body.
card_roles.Overwhelming Stampede: The alternative kill: after any board is established, +X/+X and trample where X is your best power turns even a modest board lethal. No role tag, but the function is the deck's cleanest non-Gishath finish.
card_roles.Pantlaza, Sun-Favored: The second engine, and the one that survives the wrath plan: once per turn, a Dinosaur entering discovers X equal to its toughness — no combat, no 8 mana required. Stack 001's ordering lesson exists because of this trigger: spend the discover on your biggest toughness, not your first.
card_roles.Path of Ancestry: Tapped five-colour typal land that scries every time its mana casts a Dinosaur — in a 34-Dinosaur deck it pays its tax back steadily.
card_roles.Path to Exile: Premium spot removal; the basic land it gives is cheap against a deck that wins by 20-power boards. Note it bottoms as a non-Dinosaur if Gishath reveals it (stack 001).
card_roles.Plains: Four copies backing W 9 land sources — white's pips lean on the rocks and any-colour producers.
card_roles.Polyraptor: New in v2: enrage makes a fresh 5/5 copy every time this is dealt damage. Behind Forerunner's optional trigger the verified ceiling is 7 tokens (stack 003 — bounded, self-terminating, stoppable), and in the web one ping is simply a free 5/5 that re-arms Forerunner (stack 005). It is also the card behind the bracket conversation: the combo DB's infinite tag on this pairing is what computes floor 4, and the verified stack is the counter-argument. Never pair it with the benched Marauding Raptor — stack 002 verified that loop as a mandatory whole-table draw.
card_roles.Pugnacious Hammerskull: A 6/5 for three mana whose stun-counter drawback disappears the moment you control another Dinosaur — which in this deck is nearly always.
card_roles.Quartzwood Crasher: Trample payoff: every point of trample damage your creatures deal to a player comes back as an X/X trampling token. Under Garruk's Uprising, every swing compounds.
card_roles.Ranging Raptors: New in v2: enrage ramp — whenever it's dealt damage, you may fetch a basic land onto the battlefield tapped. Verified in stack 005: one ping is one Forest, and the land entering does not re-trigger Forerunner (a Forest is not a Dinosaur). This is the web's banked value: the lands it fetches survive the wrath that erases everything else.
card_roles.Regal Behemoth: New in v2: a 5/5 trampling Dinosaur that crowns you monarch on entry and adds an extra mana every time you tap a land while you hold the crown — half of the swap block's attack on the 7.982 mean cast, with the monarch's end-step draw as a bonus. The crown is also a cost: it paints a target on you, so expect to defend it.
card_roles.Regal Imperiosaur: The typal anthem: other Dinosaurs get +1/+1, three mana. Simple multiplication across a 34-body deck.
card_roles.Regisaur Alpha: Haste for the whole tribe plus a 3/3 token on entry — the card that lets a freshly free-rolled Gishath board attack immediately. Stack 001's ordering lesson: resolve its token trigger last.
card_roles.Ripjaw Raptor: Enrage draw: every time it's dealt damage, draw a card. It draws off blocks, off Blasphemous Act (stack 004 verified the draw), and off every Forerunner ping (stack 005) — the web's card-draw spoke, now entirely maindeck.
card_roles.Rishkar's Expertise: The big refill: draw equal to your best power — routinely 7+ — then deploy a 5-drop free. The single best follow-up to a sweeper that a resolved fatty survives.
card_roles.Rogue's Passage: The connection kit's land: {4}, {T} makes Gishath unblockable. Part of the 51%-by-turn-6 evasion package that turns 'castable' into 'connects'.
card_roles.Rootbound Crag: R/G check land; untapped with a Mountain or Forest.
card_roles.Secluded Courtyard: Typal fixing done right: its any-colour mana casts Dinosaur spells AND activates abilities of Dinosaur sources — so it pays Zacama's abilities. It still cannot activate Belbe's Portal or Monster Manual (not creature sources). Read the clause, not the phrase.
card_roles.Selvala, Heart of the Wilds: New in v2 and the swap block's direct answer to the 7.982 mean cast: {G}, {T} adds X mana of any colours, where X is the greatest power among your creatures — any of the deck's 5/5s makes one activation worth five, and the goldfish models none of it. How many turns she actually shaves is unquantified until a scenario prices it. Mind the symmetry on her other ability: whoever plays the table's new biggest creature may draw, opponents included.
card_roles.Skyshroud Claim: Two Forests onto the battlefield untapped — and 'Forest' includes Canopy Vista and Cinder Glade, so it fixes all three colours while jumping two lands ahead.
card_roles.Sol Ring: The format's fastest rock; in an 8-drop deck every colourless pair matters twice.
card_roles.Sunpetal Grove: G/W check land; untapped with a Forest or Plains.
card_roles.Swords to Plowshares: The best single-target answer in the colours; the lifegain it concedes is irrelevant against your damage output.
card_roles.Talisman of Unity: G/W rock with a 1-damage sting on the coloured mode — cheap fixing for white's thin land base.
card_roles.Temple Altisaur: The asymmetry engine: all but 1 damage to your OTHER Dinosaurs is prevented. It converts Blasphemous Act into a one-sided sweep (stack 004 — where it heroically takes its own 13 and dies), and it underwrites the now-maindeck enrage web: the 1 damage it lets through is still damage dealt, so the enrage triggers keep firing while the bodies keep surviving. One blind spot by its own wording: Forerunner of the Empire is a Human, not a Dinosaur — the web's hub gets no cover here.
card_roles.Thrashing Brontodon: Instant-speed artifact/enchantment removal on a 3/4 Dinosaur body — sacrifice it in response and keep the mana open all game.
card_roles.Topiary Stomper: Ramp on a body: fetches a basic on entry; its can't-attack-until-seven-lands clause is a real cost early and no cost at all by the time this deck is swinging.
card_roles.Trapjaw Tyrant: New in v2: enrage exile — whenever it's dealt damage, exile target creature an opponent controls until this leaves the battlefield. Stack 005 verifies the repeatable removal, with its two rules edges: the target is chosen as the trigger goes on the stack (a creature already dead to the ping can never be chosen), and the exile is a hostage arrangement — the moment Trapjaw leaves, the creature comes back. A sweeper that kills Trapjaw returns its prisoners.
card_roles.Triumphant Chomp: One red mana for removal that scales with your best Dinosaur's power — 2 early, 7+ once anything real is in play. No role tag, but the function is efficient scaling spot removal.
card_roles.Trumpeting Carnosaur: Discover 5 stapled to a 7/6 trampler, with a discard mode that pings a creature or planeswalker for 3 when you need interaction instead of a body.
card_roles.Unclaimed Territory: The deck-facts trap in land form: its any-colour mana casts Dinosaur creature spells ONLY — it cannot activate Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual, or anything else. It accelerates the cast plan, never the cheat plan.
card_roles.Urza's Incubator: The headline reducer: Dinosaurs cost {2} less, turning Gishath into a six-drop and the rest of the curve into a cascade. The goldfish's 7.98 mean cast explicitly ignores this card — it is why real games run faster.
card_roles.Vaultborn Tyrant: Draw, lifegain, and insurance in one: every big body (itself included) gains 3 and draws, and it replaces itself with a copy when it dies. A wrath-math all-star.
card_roles.Wakening Sun's Avatar: The one-sided wrath on legs: destroys all non-Dinosaur creatures — but only if you CAST it from your hand, so a Gishath free-roll or a Portal activation does not trigger it. Sequence accordingly (the bench holds a spare copy). One friendly-fire note for v2: Forerunner of the Empire is not a Dinosaur, so your own Avatar cast kills your web's hub.
card_roles.Wayward Swordtooth: An extra land drop every turn, on a 5/5 that unlocks once you have the city's blessing — which a Gishath trigger grants instantly.
card_roles.Worldly Tutor: One green mana stacks any creature on top: rig the next Gishath reveal, the next Descendants' Path upkeep, or the next Etali swing. Setup, not a combo.
card_roles.Wrathful Raptors: New in v2, completing the stack-004 package in the maindeck: whenever a Dinosaur you control is dealt damage, it deals that much to any non-Dinosaur target. Under Blasphemous Act and Temple Altisaur that is a verified 16 damage redirected at a player while your board takes a 1-point haircut. How it interacts with the Forerunner ping web is deliberately unstated here — whether a ping with Wrathful out still feeds the enrage engine or converts to reach needs a stack scenario before you count on either.
card_roles.Zacama, Primal Calamity: The mana-neutral haymaker: cast it and all your lands untap, leaving mana up for its built-in removal, enchantment hate, and lifegain. Note the untap only happens if you CAST it — a Gishath free-roll gets the body and abilities, not the refund.

mulligan:
Mulligan for an engine — either engine. The goldfish's own policy — keep seven-card hands with two to five lands — kept 77.4% of hands with a mean of 0.278 mulligans, and that is your floor, not your standard. On top of the land count, demand acceleration: 87.1% of games see ramp or fixing by turn 6 (mean turn 2.0), so a keepable hand almost always has it — a hand without Cultivate, Kodama's Reach, Nature's Lore, a rock, a dork, or Selvala is below your deck's average and should usually go back. The reason is the naked number the ramp exists to fix: Gishath's mean cast is turn 7.982, and only 8.8% of goldfish games cast him by turn 6.

What v2 changes is that a second kind of hand became keepable: the web curve. Forerunner of the Empire plus any cheap Dinosaur — Itzquinth, Ranging Raptors, Ripjaw Raptor — is now a real game plan on its own, and the deck delivers it: enrage pieces are drawn by turn 6 in 72.1% of games (mean turn 2.6), the single largest number the swap block moved. Stack 005 prices what that hand does every turn while Gishath waits: removal, ramp, draw, and bodies off one optional ping. Still prize the cheat/reducer layer above raw ramp when you can get both — Urza's Incubator, Otepec Huntmaster, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual, or Descendants' Path shows up by turn 6 in only 56.5% of games, the deck's scarcest resource. Protection (49.3% by turn 6) and the connection kit (50.9%) are keep bonuses, not requirements. Ship: hands that are all payoff (two or more 5+ drops and no acceleration — mean available mana at turn 6 is just 5.497, and the land-drop hit rate has already fallen to 52.4% by then, so the deck does not organically climb to eight), and hands whose only lands are Unclaimed Territory plus tapped duals, which can't deploy a turn-two rock or Signet on time. A dork-heavy keep is fine but fragile: dorks are ramp that dies to the sweepers this deck most fears, so keep one land-based ramp piece alongside them when you can.
upgrades:
V2's upgrade section is a history, not a shopping list, because the upgrade already happened — and the way it happened is the lesson. Nothing moved off the bench until a checker-passed stack said what it actually did: five verifications first, seven swaps after, one branch refused. Stack 001 priced the core engine on a real board. Stack 002 asked whether Marauding Raptor + Polyraptor was the free infinite the combo database promises and got the answer that shaped everything: a mandatory whole-table DRAW-machine — every trigger forced, the 2-damage ping never lethal to a fresh 5/5, no exit anywhere in the deck, CR 732.4 / 104.4b ending the game for everyone if no opponent intervenes. Stack 003 verified the same Polyraptor engine behind Forerunner of the Empire's OPTIONAL trigger as bounded: max 7 tokens, self-terminating, safe to stop at every link. Stack 004 verified Wrathful Raptors converting Blasphemous Act under Temple Altisaur into a one-sided sweep with 16 redirected at a player. Stack 005 then re-verified the whole ping web on the exact board the proposed block would create — one ping yielding exile, ramp, draw, and a re-arming copy token.

On that evidence the block was applied (HISTORY.md, 2026-07-28, decklist fb99de15993a). In: Selvala, Heart of the Wilds, Regal Behemoth, Forerunner of the Empire, Polyraptor, Wrathful Raptors, Ranging Raptors, Trapjaw Tyrant. Out to the bench: Ravenous Sailback, Verdant Sun's Avatar, Goring Ceratops, Zetalpa, Primal Dawn, Earthshaker Dreadmaw, Drover of the Mighty, and Kinjalli's Sunwing — seven fair-value or redundant bodies traded for a verified second engine plus the acceleration the 7.982 mean cast demanded. And the branch not taken: swap eight would have been Marauding Raptor, and it was declined BECAUSE of stack 002's verdict. It stays benched under a warning label — never promote it without first adding a loop-breaker you control, because until then its Polyraptor pairing is a liability wearing a wincon's clothes.

The price on paper is the honest footnote: the computed bracket floor moved from 3 to 4 solely on the combo DB tagging Polyraptor + Forerunner infinite — the same pairing stack 003 verified as bounded at seven tokens. The engine does not yet consult passing stacks, so the report presents 4; the verified-reality argument is 3, and the pregame conversation is where you make it, stack in hand.

What remains on the bench is tech and spares, not a queue: Marauding Raptor under its warning, a spare Wakening Sun's Avatar beside the maindeck copy, graveyard and meta options like Deathgorge Scavenger and Runic Armasaur, and further enrage bodies (Bellowing Aegisaur, Frilled Deathspitter, Apex Altisaur) for tables where the web wants depth. The remaining card-by-card conditional reads render from the sideboard-analysis artifact rather than being restated here. For the maindeck itself, the obsolescence index still offers little tuned to typal fit; its one actionable note remains the strict ramp family (it lists Three Visits and Farseek beside the Nature's Lore / Skyshroud Claim class already here).
threat_assessment: Start with the sit-down conversation, because v2 changed your label: the bracket report now computes a floor of 4, and you owe the table the honest version of why. Say it plainly: 'The report says 4 because the combo database tags Polyraptor plus Forerunner of the Empire as a two-card infinite. Our own checker resolved that pairing on the exact board (stack 003, passed): it is bounded — a maximum of 7 tokens, and only by declining one intermediate trigger; every link has a safe stop and the chain self-terminates when Forerunner dies. The genuinely unbounded partner, Marauding Raptor, is deliberately NOT in the deck, because stack 002 verified that pairing as a mandatory loop that draws the whole game.' Present the 4, argue the verified-reality 3, and let the table decide — never sandbag the label and then drop seven raptors on turn six. On the clock: the table still counts to eight. Goldfish v2 mean cast is 7.982, median 8, only 8.8% by turn 6 — Selvala, Heart of the Wilds and Regal Behemoth attack that number (Selvala taps for X equal to your greatest power, 5+ once any of your 5/5s lands; Behemoth adds a mana on every land tap while you hold the crown), and ramp or fixing is in hand by turn 6 in 87% of games (mean turn 2.0). But the bigger v2 change is WHAT the table now fears: v1 was ignorable until seven mana; v2 becomes a problem the moment Forerunner of the Empire stands next to any raptor, because stack 005 verified what one Dinosaur ETB then buys — one optional ping kills a 1/1, exiles their best creature under Trapjaw Tyrant, draws off Ripjaw, fetches a land with Ranging Raptors, and copies Polyraptor, with the new 5/5 offering a fresh ping you may decline. The enrage engine is drawn by turn 6 in 72% of games now (up from 49%), and experienced tables answer it at the hub: Forerunner is a 1/3 HUMAN SOLDIER, outside every tribal shield — Temple Altisaur's prevention names Dinosaurs, and the typal lands cannot even cast him. Expect him to eat the first Swords on sight; deploy him the turn you can use him, not before, or bait the removal first. Two new signal costs: Regal Behemoth's crown paints an attack-me target the turn it resolves, and Selvala's biggest-power draw feeds opponents' fatties too — sequence her when your own curve dominates the board. The recast-tax discipline survives v2 softened, not repealed: 8 becomes 10 becomes 12, and Selvala/Behemoth make the 10 reachable a turn sooner, but every uncovered answer still costs the tempo turn — so the swing still waits for cover, and Flawless Maneuver (free with the commander out) is still the swing-turn card. The table cannot know you hold it: protection is in hand by turn 6 in only 49% of games, and that ambiguity is armor. Passage-versus-pump is unchanged: the trigger reveals cards equal to damage dealt, so Kessig Wolf Run grows the reveal only if it lands — Rogue's Passage beats the pump whenever a real blocker exists (a 4-toughness chump shaves the reveal from 7 to 3 through trample; a deathtouch block kills the commander and hands you the tax). And the moment the trigger banks (stack 001: five bodies, three draws, a discover at X=6), stop posturing — you are the archenemy, the ping web is your board control, and the plan is to end the game within one rotation.
matchups: VS SWEEPER CONTROL — still the worst frame: the Gishath board arrives as one wrath-sized package, so deploy-in-waves remains structurally unavailable. But v2 has a real consolation: the ping web is the rebuild engine that works the turn after the wrath — enrage pieces are in hand by turn 6 in 72% of games (mean turn 2.6), and one Dinosaur ETB through Forerunner re-buys removal, ramp, and a body (stack 005). You hold protection in 49% of games by turn 6; know which spell beats which wrath: Flawless Maneuver (free with commander out) and Boros Charm answer destroy-based sweepers; Heroic Intervention adds hexproof; Akroma's Will with commander out gives indestructible plus protection from each color; Eerie Interlude is the only out to -X/-X, sacrifice, and exile wraths — but it abandons tokens (Polyraptor copies included) and is the desperation line. Note the board-wide instants now carry a second duty: they are the only cover Forerunner of the Empire has, because Temple Altisaur's shield names Dinosaurs and he is a Human Soldier. And with Wrathful Raptors now maindeck, YOUR Blasphemous Act is a verified one-sided sweep (stack 004: your Dinosaurs are dealt 1 each under Temple Altisaur, 16 redirected at a player) — but Act deals Forerunner the full 13, so the web's hub dies to your own wrath; fire it as a reset, not mid-engine. VS FASTER COMBO — still the bad seat: zero counterspells in Naya, mean cast 7.982 with 8.8% by turn 6, and a clock that starts around turn 7. What changed: the bounded burst (stack 003, max 7 tokens on your terms) plus the web means your pressure no longer waits for the commander — a turn-5 Forerunner-plus-Polyraptor board threatens real damage a full rotation before Gishath. Answer-economy still governs: the 6 spot-removal slots go at enablers on sight, Trumpeting Carnosaur's discard mode is instant-speed reach, and the cheat layer (56% of games have a reducer or cheat piece by turn 6) is the race plan — Belbe's Portal deploys Gishath at instant speed the end step before your combat. VS STAX — taxes hit an 8-drop hardest, and the fight is still over your cheat layer: mulligan toward Incubator/Portal/Monster Manual/Descendants' Path on the 56% figure. Selvala is your best mana under stax — one activation, one card, X equal to your greatest power — and dorks ignore land-punishment pieces. Aim Thrashing Brontodon, Beast Within, and Austere Command at the piece that turns off the cheat layer specifically. The deck-facts trap stands: Unclaimed Territory's mana casts creature spells only — it cannot activate Portal or Monster Manual, and neither typal land casts the non-Dinosaur Forerunner. VS ENRAGE-HOSTILE BOARDS (deathtouch and first-strike tables) — v2 inverts this matchup. Combat enrage is still a trap there: Temple Altisaur's prevention leaves 1 damage through and 1 deathtouch damage still destroys, so never offer Ripjaw or Polyraptor as attackers into deathtouch blocks. But the web IS the answer: Forerunner's ping deals your creatures 1 from YOUR source — their deathtouchers never touch it — Trapjaw's enrage exiles their deathtoucher outright, and Rogue's Passage dodges the block entirely. One husbandry rule: the ping hits Forerunner himself (1 of 3, verified in stack 005), so three pings in one turn kill your own hub — count before you say yes a third time.
